pieces.name: Chicken in a party hat
pieces.caption: Happy New Ur's street Chickens wear party hats on December 31 and January 1. Glitch never dressed its animals, so this is new, but nothing in it is newly drawn: Tiny Speck's own party hat, the one Glitches wore, sits on Tiny Speck's own Chicken, inside its rig, so it walks, pecks, flaps and sits in it.

image.label: Made for Groddle
image.alt: A white Chicken standing with a small blue party hat dotted with gold stars and a gold pompom on top of its head.

original.alt: Tiny Speck's white Chicken standing, with its small red comb and short dark tail.
original.label: Tiny Speck's Chicken, the drawing it is made from

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: Made by Claude, putting Tiny Speck's own party hat on Tiny Speck's own chicken drawing, under Austin's direction: the hat's own shapes and colours from Tiny Speck's party hat, set on the Chicken's comb, so every pose of the original carries it.

facts.label: How it was checked
facts.text: The plain Chicken drawn the same way matches Tiny Speck's own pictures frame by frame, so the hat rides exactly where the head does.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: Every Chicken out on the streets wears one on December 31 and January 1, for everyone.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it is made from.

pieces.name: Coral Caves' crystals, spires and kelp
pieces.caption: Coral Caves, one of the home street styles: a sandy sea floor in murky olive light, with rocks, beaded branches, fiddleheads and an old boat. The street itself was never saved, only its small header picture from 2012. Most of its pieces are Tiny Speck's own, found in other streets, but nothing in Tiny Speck's files matches its dark and pale crystal clusters, its tall pale spires or its curling kelp stalks, so those four were drawn again.

image.label: With the pictures made for Groddle
image.alt: A murky olive sea floor: tall wavy kelp stalks with curled tips behind the rocks, pale banded stone spires, black-green crystal clusters with bright green edges by the boat and on the sand, among beaded branches and fiddleheads.

original.alt: The same street before: rocks, beaded branches, fiddleheads, mushrooms and the boat, with no crystals, spires or kelp.
original.label: Before

facts.label: What the 2012 street had
facts.text: Clusters of dark crystals with pale ones beside them out on the sand, tall pale spires standing behind them, and wavy kelp stalks rising behind the rocks, as the header picture and players' pictures show.

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: Drawn by an image model (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst) for Austin, one picture for each piece, from our drawing of their sizes, three crops of the 2012 header and Tiny Speck's own pieces from the street for the look. They are drawn in natural colours, and the street tints them olive with everything else.

facts.label: How it was checked
facts.text: Each piece was measured against the boat in the header and placed where it shows them: the spires and kelp behind the rocks, the crystals among them and on the sand in front, a pale cluster beside every second dark one. The street was looked at in the game before and after.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: Your home street, in the Coral Caves style (Change Style by your house).

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it comes from.

pieces.name: Cloud Rings' cloud hoops
pieces.caption: Cloud Rings, a Ticket to Paradise course: you fly through a sunset sky, over purple mountains and a sea of lavender cloud, and through tall hoops of cloud standing on their edge. The course itself was never saved, only players' pictures of it from 2012. Its clouds and mountains are Tiny Speck's own pieces from other streets, but nothing in Tiny Speck's files matches the hoops, so one was drawn again. The game tints it lavender, and gold once you have flown through.

image.label: With the picture made for Groddle
image.alt: A sunset sky, violet at the top fading to orange and gold, purple mountains along the horizon and lavender cloud below, with a tall lavender hoop of crinkly cloud standing on its edge, its opening on the left.

original.alt: The same course before: a dark teal night sky with rings of bright yellow, orange, purple and blue ovals hanging in loops.
original.label: Drawn in plain shapes

facts.label: What the 2012 course had
facts.text: Eight tall hoops of cloud along a long sunset sky, each about twice as tall as wide with its opening on the left, all lavender until you flew through them and gold after, as players' pictures of the whole course show.

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: Drawn by an image model (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst) for Austin, in white and grey so the game can tint it, from our drawing of its size, two crops of the players' pictures of the course and Tiny Speck's own clouds for the look.

facts.label: How it was checked
facts.text: The hoop was measured against the players' pictures, 165 by 330, and its opening is where you pass it. The course was flown in the game before and after.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: Cloud Rings, from a Ticket To Cloud Rings.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it comes from.

pieces.name: Le Voyage Violet's stump and spiral stone
pieces.caption: Le Voyage Violet, the dream room an Essence of Purple sends you to: washing on lines under a crescent moon, mushrooms, a sleeping owl and a shy ghost, all in violet light. The room itself was never saved, only players' snapshots of it from 2012. Its mushrooms, frond heads, ferns, ghost and owl are Tiny Speck's own pieces from Uralia, but nothing in Tiny Speck's files matches the tall cut stumps with wax dripping over their tops or the carved spiral stone, so those two were drawn again.

image.label: With the pictures made for Groddle
image.alt: A violet room: a tall cut stump with pale wax dripping over its top, a rounded stone carved with a square spiral, red umbrella mushrooms, a sleeping owl on a washing line and black fern shapes in front of lilac peaks.

original.alt: The same room before: small flat purple stumps, a spiral drawn as a line on an oval, and leaf-shaped fronds in front of the peaks.
original.label: Drawn in plain shapes

facts.label: What the 2012 room had
facts.text: Stumps taller than a player, flat-topped and dripping, a carved stone about as wide as a player is tall, red and lilac mushrooms, a ghost peeping over a boulder and an owl asleep on the washing line, as players' snapshots show.

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: Drawn by an image model (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst) for Austin, one chat for the stump and one for the stone, from our drawing of their sizes, three crops of the players' 2012 snapshots and Tiny Speck's own Uralia pieces for the look. The stone came back a little wide and was narrowed. Both are drawn in natural colours, and the room tints them violet with everything else.

facts.label: How it was checked
facts.text: Each piece was measured against the player in the snapshots and placed as they show it. The room was walked in the game on a computer and a phone, in both looks, its floor and its Scions unchanged.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: The Purple Journey: imbibe an Essence of Purple and wait a minute.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it comes from.

pieces.name: The Outer Mind
pieces.caption: The Outer Mind, the second part of Gwendolyn's Task, where you walk through your own head: a rock-rimmed head floating in space with a sunburst brain, glass eyes, and one long pink tube that runs from a giant foot on a checkered floor up and across into an eye. None of its pictures survive in Tiny Speck's files, only in players' snapshots from 2012, so the head, the eyes, the tube, the foot and the floor were drawn again, and the room was laid out again in the snapshots' shape.

image.label: With the pictures made for Groddle
image.alt: A giant head of cracked grey rock with an orange and pink sunburst inside, three glassy blue eyes, and a pink tube looping from a pink foot on a cyan and white checkered floor into the right-hand eye.

original.alt: The same room before: a flat orange and pink sunburst, white cartoon eyes and straight pink bars stacked in tiers over a grey floor.
original.label: Drawn in plain shapes

facts.label: What the 2012 room had
facts.text: A head about as tall as it was wide, its rim cracked rock, the sunburst dense and three-coloured, two eyes at the top and a third whose socket took the tube, and one tube winding from the foot up to it, as players' snapshots show.

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: Drawn by an image model (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst) for Austin, one chat for each piece, from our drawing of their sizes, three of the players' 2012 snapshots and Tiny Speck's own pieces from the Inner Mind next door. The head was drawn wide and pressed to the snapshots' shape. The tube was drawn as one straight stretch that repeats, and the game bends it along the whole path.

facts.label: How it was checked
facts.text: The room was measured from the snapshots by the player's height and laid out in their shape: up the foot, a hop at each turn, along the top to the squid. It was played through on a computer and a phone, in both looks.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: Gwendolyn's Task, part two, in Jethimadh's tower from level 12, and every time the task is taken again.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it comes from.

facts.label: How it was checked

pieces.name: Winter Walk's tree arch and curling plants
pieces.caption: The big hollow tree arch and the pale green curling plants of Winter Walk, the snowy street a street spirit sends you down from level 7. The arch is two old trees whose branches cross overhead, with the walk's line about icicles written inside it. No picture of either survives in Tiny Speck's files, only in players' snapshots of the street from 2012, so they were made again. Each plant is two or three copies of one stalk, turned and mirrored, as the snapshots show a clump of curls.

image.label: Made for Groddle
image.alt: Two bare grey-brown trees leaning together so their branches cross in an arch, a dark hollow in the right trunk and snow on the roots; beside them a clump of three pale green curling stalks and a low pair creeping along the ground.

facts.label: What the 2012 street had
facts.text: A snowy wood of tall dead trees. Past the camp, two gnarled trees leaned together into an arch with the line about icicles inside it, and pale green stalks curled up out of the snow beside it and along the walk.

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: Drawn by an image model (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst) for Austin, one chat for the arch and one for the plants. It was given our drawing of the sizes, three of the players' 2012 snapshots to look at, and Tiny Speck's own trees from the street to match the look. Austin chose the arch; of two tries, the first kept the two trees apart, as the snapshots do.

facts.label: How it was checked
facts.text: The arch was sized by its opening, so the line about icicles fits between the trunks as it does in the snapshots. The street was walked in the game on a desktop and a phone, in both looks, its floor, icicles and pillars unchanged.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: Winter Walk, offered by the street spirits from level 7, and its repeat.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it comes from.

pieces.name: Winter Walk

facts.label: How it was made

pieces.name: Winter Haven's snowy trees
pieces.caption: The three snowy trees of Winter Haven, the cave at the end of Winter Walk: the branches reaching in at both sides and the trees by the exit ladder. Tiny Speck's files have the bare trees but not their snow, which only players' pictures of the haven from 2013 show, so the trees were drawn again with snow along their branches and a few short icicles.

image.label: Made for Groddle
image.alt: Three dark bare trees, a tall single one, a taller forked one and a group of four, with white snow along the tops of their branches and short icicles hanging under them.

original.alt: The same three Tiny Speck trees, bare, at the same heights.
original.label: Tiny Speck's bare trees

facts.label: What the haven had
facts.text: Bare dead trees reaching in from the cave's edges, every branch capped with snow, as four players' pictures of the haven from early 2013 show.

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: Drawn by an image model (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst) for Austin. It was given each Tiny Speck tree and asked only to add snow; it drew each tree again instead, close to the original but not the same, so they count as new pictures rather than Tiny Speck's own.

facts.label: How it was checked
facts.text: Each tree stands as tall as the Tiny Speck tree it replaces, a little wider, its root on the same spot. The haven was climbed in the game on a computer and a phone, in both looks, its rubble, pillars and ladder unchanged.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: Winter Haven, the second street of Winter Walk, offered by the street spirits from level 7, and its repeat.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it comes from.

pieces.name: Walk Toward the Light's dishes, shades, poles and ledges
pieces.caption: The dish platforms, ceiling lamp shades, striped poles and stone ledges of Walk Toward the Light, the second puzzle level a player meets. No picture of them survives in Tiny Speck's files, only in players' snapshots of the room from 2012, so they were made again. The dish and the pole are grey on purpose: the room tints one picture by the light it stands in, as the snapshots show the same dish in six colours.

image.label: Made for Groddle
image.alt: A dark dotted lamp shade, a grey dish platform with a cratered top and two smaller copies tinted yellow and blue, a red striped pole with a round cap, and a long dark stone ledge with angled ends.

facts.label: What the 2012 room had
facts.text: A dark room where lamp shades hang from the ceiling and throw soft cones of coloured light; shallow dishes that appear only in light of their own colour; red and pink striped columns that stand while a red light shines; and dark stone ledges to start from.

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: Drawn by an image model (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst) for Austin, one piece at a time. It was given our drawing of the sizes, three of the players' 2012 snapshots to look at, and a sheet of Tiny Speck's own art from these rooms to match the look. Austin chose the pictures.

facts.label: How it was checked
facts.text: Each picture was measured against the drawing. The dish was made 16% flatter to the drawing's shape, the ledge's ends were narrowed to it and the pole's segments overlap a little so they stack without a gap. The room was played in the game on a desktop and a phone, in both looks, its platforms, walls and puzzle unchanged.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: Walk Toward the Light, offered at level 6, and its replay. The dish and the ledge also stand in Radiant Glare.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it comes from.

pieces.caption: The same stretch of the room before and after, at its last lesson: two always-on lamps over their dishes and a red striped wall between them. Until the new pieces came, the shades, dishes, poles and ledges were drawn in plain shapes.

image.alt: A dark room: a stone ledge with a ladder, orange and yellow dishes in soft cones of light, dark dotted lamp shades and a red striped pole.

pieces.name: Radiant Glare's spotlights, bulbs and knobs
pieces.caption: The wall spotlights, the caged switch bulbs and the pipe knobs of the light puzzles. The spotlights light Radiant Glare's tall shaft; the bulbs and knobs make up the switch rigs of both Radiant Glare and Walk Toward the Light. Like the dishes, they survive only in players' snapshots from 2012. The bulbs are pale on purpose, so each one can be tinted red, yellow or blue, and lit.

image.label: Made for Groddle
image.alt: A dark perforated spotlight dish seen edge on with two pale bulbs and a wall bracket, caged glass bulbs lit in red, yellow, blue and white with soft halos, the same bulbs unlit below, and a dark round knob.

facts.label: What the 2012 room had
facts.text: A dark shaft climbed floor by floor toward a rainbow, lit from the walls by perforated spotlights, with stone consoles carrying rows of red, yellow and blue caged bulbs on pipes joined at round knobs.

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: Drawn by an image model (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst) for Austin, one piece at a time, from our drawing of the sizes, players' 2012 snapshots of the room and close crops of them, and Tiny Speck's own art to match the look. The two bulbs came back in one picture and were cut apart; the unlit bulb's grey glass was lightened so its tint reads true.

facts.label: How it was checked
facts.text: Each picture was measured against the drawing and compared with the snapshots. The room was played in the game on a desktop and a phone, in both looks, its floors, platforms and puzzle unchanged.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: Radiant Glare, offered at level 7, and its replay; the bulbs and knobs also on Walk Toward the Light's switches.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it comes from.

pieces.name: Groddle Meadow map
pieces.caption: The painted background of the Groddle Meadow region map. Tiny Speck's full-size map paintings are lost as files, but the 2012 Encyclopedia drew this one at full size under the game's roads and street names. That picture was restored: the markings taken off and the painting sharpened, with everything else left where Tiny Speck put it.

image.label: Restored from 2012
image.alt: A painted top-down view of Groddle Meadow: rolling green fields, small trees and bushes, a flower patch and rocks, a cliff along the top edge and a forest at the right.

original.alt: Tiny Speck's small thumbnail of the same map, enlarged so its pixels show: the same fields and trees, blurred.
original.label: Tiny Speck's thumbnail, 150 by 91 pixels, shown at the same size

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: Restored by an image model (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst) under Austin's direction, from the 2012 Encyclopedia's picture of this map: asked to remove only the roads, names, icons and GO buttons and sharpen, without moving anything. Its colour was then brought back to the 2012 picture's.

facts.label: How it was chosen
facts.text: Austin compared it with the 2012 picture and with the painting made earlier from the thumbnail, and chose the restore. Every other region's map was then restored the same way, so all 51 show Tiny Speck's own painting.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: The background of the Groddle Meadow map. The game draws its own streets, names and markers on top.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it comes from.

pieces.name: EZ Cookin' counters, lamps and table
pieces.caption: The glass serving counters, the white lamps over them and the round mosaic table of Breezy, EZ Cookin', the forest street where the EZ Cooking quest begins. No picture of them survives in Tiny Speck's files, only in players' snapshots of the street from 2012, so they were made again from their measured sizes.

image.label: Made for Groddle
image.alt: The made pieces at the same sizes: a mosaic-topped table on scrolled grey iron legs, a pale aqua glass lid over a white steel counter, and a white drum lamp hanging on four wires.

original.alt: Plain outlines of a round table, a glass-topped counter and a drum lamp hanging over it, at their measured sizes.
original.label: Our drawing of their sizes, measured from the 2012 snapshots

facts.label: What the 2012 street had
facts.text: Three glass-topped serving counters in a row along a pine forest lane at sunset, the food laid out on the glass, a white drum lamp hanging over each, and a small round table with a tiled top where the Knife & Board waited.

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: Drawn by an image model (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst) for Austin, one piece at a time. It was given our drawing of the sizes and four sheets of Tiny Speck's own glass, tables, lamps and forest art to match the look, and a description of each piece in words. Austin chose the pictures.

facts.label: How it was checked
facts.text: Each picture was measured against the drawing: the counter is within 3% of its shape, the lamp within 6% and the table within 8%. The food was set on the counters and the Knife & Board on the table where the street's own script puts them, and the street was walked in the game on a desktop and a phone, in both looks.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: Breezy, EZ Cookin', when you take its quest or pick EZ Cooking in the tutorial.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it comes from.

pieces.name: Breezy, EZ Cookin'
pieces.caption: The same stretch of the street before and after. Until the new pieces came, Tiny Speck pieces that were close enough stood in: a shop counter for each serving counter, a hanging shop lamp over each, and a wooden pedestal table. The shop lamps looked too much like swings, so for a while the street had no lamps at all.

image.label: With the pieces made for Groddle
image.alt: The forest lane with two glass-topped white counters, bread, cheese and meat on them, and a white drum lamp over each.

original.alt: The same forest lane with beige shop counters on red legs, the same food on them, and green shop lamps hanging over them.
original.label: With Tiny Speck's stand-ins

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: The counters, lamps and table are by an image model (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst). Everything else on the street is Tiny Speck's own art, laid out where the 2012 snapshots show it.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: Both pictures are the game itself: the tutorial's EZ Cooking practice street, the food where the street's script lays it.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it comes from.

pieces.name: Subway map paper
pieces.caption: The paper under the Subway System map: pale sage green with cream sheets laid on it. Tiny Speck's full-size paper is lost. It survives only as the little map on the in-world Subway Map sign, so it was made again.

image.label: Made again for Groddle, the game's line drawn on it
image.alt: The recreated paper: cream sheets on soft sage green paper with faint fold creases, the red line and its stations drawn over it.

original.alt: The little map on Tiny Speck's Subway Map sign, enlarged so its pixels show: cream sheets on pale green, a purple line with round stops.
original.label: The map on Tiny Speck's Subway Map sign, 232 by 158 pixels, shown at the same height

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: Painted by an image model (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst) for Austin from our drawing of where the twelve sheets lie, measured from a 2012 picture of the map window, with the sign, Tiny Speck's world map charts and the station signs to match its look. It was asked for paper only: no line, no names.

facts.label: How it was checked
facts.text: Each sheet's edges were found and compared with the drawing, then the picture was gently stretched to line them up. After that, nearly every edge sits within one unit of where it belongs.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: The Subway view of the Map. The game draws the line, the stations and their names on top.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it comes from.

pieces.name: World map
pieces.caption: Tiny Speck's World map, sharpened for Retina screens. Tiny Speck drew its two charts, the painted one and the sketched one, only 760 by 460 pixels, and the World view shows them much larger on a sharp screen, where they looked soft. These are the same charts at twice the size: every coast, route and hand-lettered name where it was.

image.label: Sharpened for Groddle, twice the size
image.alt: The painted World map, crisp: dark blue sea, Groddle Isle and its neighbours in soft painted colours, the islands' names in Tiny Speck's own hand.

original.alt: Tiny Speck's painted World map: the same sea, islands and names, softer and a little blocky.
original.label: Tiny Speck's painted chart, 760 by 460 pixels, shown at the same size

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: Sharpened by an image model (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst) for Austin, one chart at a time, each asked to move and redraw nothing, only to take away the blur. A first try that redrew islands and lettering was thrown away.

facts.label: How it was checked
facts.text: Laid over Tiny Speck's charts and nudged onto their lines, then matched to their colours. Every part of each map sits within one pixel of where it is on the original, at the original's size. A few marks read more clearly than before: the dashed routes, a faint line beside Groddle Isle on the sketched chart, a small tick on the compass.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: The World view of the Map on a Retina screen or a phone, and on any screen once the map is shown larger than 760 by 460. The region frames, cards and your star sit where they always did.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it comes from.

pieces.name: Quest book
pieces.caption: The open book on the card you see when you finish a quest. Tiny Speck drew it only 86 by 58 pixels, which turned soft and blurry when the card showed it large, so it was redrawn bigger to match the original as closely as possible.

image.label: Redrawn for Groddle
image.alt: The redrawn quest book: an open book with cream pages, a red cover and an orange bookmark, sharp at this size.

original.alt: Tiny Speck's quest book, enlarged so its pixels show: the same open book, blocky and soft.
original.label: Tiny Speck's original, 86 by 58 pixels, shown at the same size

facts.label: How it was made
facts.text: Redrawn by an image model (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst) under Austin's direction, with Tiny Speck's own 86 by 58 book enlarged twelve times as the guide.

facts.label: How it was checked
facts.text: Shrunk back down to 86 by 58 pixels, its outline overlaps the original's by 96%.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: The card for a finished quest in the Modern look. The Classic look keeps Tiny Speck's original book.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, like the Tiny Speck art it comes from.

ours.name: Stat icons
ours.caption: One icon and one colour for each stat, the same in the top bar, in speech bubbles, in the amounts that float up and on the reward card. Glitch drew each stat its own way in each place: a bolt beside the energy gauge, a green battery in a speech bubble. A player asked for one of each, so these were drawn for Groddle in its flat style, each after the Tiny Speck picture it stands in for. Later the same player asked for Tiny Speck's pictures back; Austin kept ours and gave the coin the two strokes of Tiny Speck's currant sign.

image.label: Ours, in the same order
image.alt: Our six stat icons in two rows: an orange bolt, a green smile and a blue star on discs, a purple i, a gold coin with a crossed C and a plum star.

original.label: Tiny Speck's speech bubble pictures, energy, mood, XP, iMG, currants and favor
original.alt: Tiny Speck's six small stat pictures in two rows: a green battery, a green smile, a teal xp disc, a purple i, a brown coin with a crossed C and a maroon star.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: The modern look shows these everywhere a stat appears. The classic look keeps Tiny Speck's own pictures.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: Ours, drawn by the game's own code under the project's MIT licence. The Tiny Speck pictures beside them are CC0 1.0.

ours.name: Reimagined clothes
ours.caption: Tiny Speck left 19 clothing files as greyscale masters that Glitch never sold, so they never had colours. Groddle sells them in colours borrowed from the piece they match, or chosen from the same palette where none does, and marks them Reimagined in the wardrobe. The drawing is Tiny Speck's; only the colours are ours.

image.label: Ours, in the colours we gave them
image.alt: The same two Glitches: the banana hat now yellow, the teapot dress blue and white with gold trim.

original.label: Tiny Speck's files as they are, in greyscale
original.alt: A Glitch in a white banana hat beside one in a white teapot dress, both drawn in greys.

facts.label: In the game
facts.text: Each one is sold and worn like any other piece of clothing, with a Reimagined tag that says where its colours come from.

facts.label: Licence
facts.text: The drawing is Tiny Speck's, under CC0 1.0; only the colours are ours, set in the game's own data.
